title: Cooling specifications — 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
This reference separates coolant identity, fill capacity, mixture concentration, freeze protection, pressure and thermostat behavior. I read those labels before the figures: they are different instruments in the same cooling-system orchestra, and a pressure limit cannot play the thermostat’s part.

Match each coolant’s product description, identifier and specification. Keep the dedicated coolant-mixture entry separate from the freeze-protection examples, whose percentages run coolant first and distilled water second. Retain the displayed volume, pressure and temperature units. This page provides specifications rather than coolant-changeover, mixing, filling or testing procedures, and it does not establish permission to mix coolant types.

edits.why: Use the product description, identifier and specification as a set. Concentrated and prediluted coolant have separate entries, even where their capacity entries agree. Capacity alone does not explain how to prepare a mixture.

These rows identify service coolant products and the separate flushing material. Keep each product with its own specification and capacity entry. The flush row’s dash supplies no quantity, and the service listing does not describe a coolant changeover.

Each percentage pair describes coolant relative to distilled water and leads to its corresponding freeze-protection temperature. Preserve the extreme-cold qualifier when reading that row. These examples describe protection at particular proportions; the dedicated mixture entry below remains a separate specification.

This entry states the coolant mixture with water. I keep it distinct from total system capacity and from the freeze-protection examples above. It supplies a concentration specification, not a preparation sequence for either concentrated or prediluted product.

Choose the row that matches the complete system, relief cap or radiator removed from the vehicle. Those qualifiers determine which specification applies. A pressure figure supplies neither the test connections nor the conditions and observations needed to judge a test.

The thermostat controls the coolant path through the radiator. Starting to open and reaching fully open describe different valve positions during warming, so keep each stage with its listed temperature and unit. Neither entry alone is a complete thermostat test.
